description:
EMPIRICAL FINDINGS (tested live 2026-05-22):

1. Sub-agents CAN load custom skills IFF granted the Skill tool. Tested: general-purpose (tools: *) loaded custom skill credential-discipline successfully; CAPTAIN_ADA (default grant Bash/Read/Write/Edit/Grep/Glob/WebSearch/WebFetch, no Skill) could not - no Skill tool in its surface. So it is a tool-grant config WE control, NOT a platform limit.

2. Agent definitions are cached at session start. A mid-session edit to an agent .md is NOT picked up without a restart (or the /agents UI). So in-session edit-and-redispatch tests are inconclusive.

3. Two grant mechanisms (per docs): tools: ..., Skill (on-demand, can invoke any skill) and a skills: frontmatter field (named skills injected at the sub-agent's startup).

4. CONSTRAINT: a skill that itself dispatches agents BREAKS inside a sub-agent (sub-agents cannot spawn sub-sub-agents - GitHub issues #59968, #19077). Pure-reference skills are safe; orchestration skills are not.

5. DISCIPLINE (PRINCIPAL): never run config/grant experiments on real or canonical agent files. Use a disposable dummy agent, then delete it. Final decided changes only ever go to substrate source + redeploy. (Logged after I added Skill to a real CAPTAIN_ADA.md to test - reverted, but the act was the error.)

NOTE: given the CLI-not-MCP decision (bw delivery via Bash), the Skill-grant question is moot for bw - but these facts govern any future use of the Anthropic Skill mechanism.
title: Finding: skill-grant reachability + agent-def caching + no-experiments-on-real-agents
